facts.text: Vidalia’s name probably comes from a daughter of railroad president Samuel Hawkins, tying the town’s origin to the rail line.
In 1931 Mose Coleman noticed his onions were sweeter, launching the Vidalia onion that would later be named Georgia’s official vegetable in 1990.
The Altama Museum of Art & History, housed in the 1911 Brazell House, displays 18th‑century American and European prints and porcelain.
Vidalia once hosted the Vidalia Indians, a Class D minor league baseball team that won the 1953 Georgia State League championship.
The Vidalia Onion Factory café and gift shop sells onion products year‑round, keeping the town’s famous crop alive beyond its harvest season.
